questions.question: Describe the staircase that every walked question in this practice set climbs, and state where the paragraph task fits and how it is credited.
questions.expected_answer: Each walked question opens with a two-mark definition, moves into reading the source — a chart, sketch, extract or table — then stacks explanation questions above that, and closes with a paragraph task where insight lives. In this practice set the paragraph carries eight marks, credited as four ideas at two marks each: the first mark of each pair for stating the idea, the second for developing it with a because-clause, and full sentences are compulsory throughout.

questions.question: Using the Cyclone Denga walkthrough, explain how mark allocations should control the length of your answers, with examples.
questions.expected_answer: The allocation is the instruction for length: the one-times-two identification of the tropical cyclone needs one precise line; the two-times-two summer-evidence question needs two developed facts, such as the highs sitting south of their winter positions and the very existence of a late-summer cyclone; the three-times-two description of the coming weather needs three developed sentences covering destructive winds, torrential spiral-band rain with flooding, and the storm surge. Writing a paragraph for a two-mark item wastes time, and writing one line for a six-mark item abandons marks.

questions.question: Write out the four-move recipe for a paragraph task and apply it to the drought and food-security task from the lesson.
questions.expected_answer: Move one: obey the instruction verb — here 'suggest', which demands workable solutions. Move two: plan four ideas as margin keywords, such as climate-smart farming, small-farmer support, water banking, and school feeding. Move three: write one full sentence per idea and develop each with a because-clause — for example, promote drought-resistant seed and minimum tillage because they hold yields when rain fails. Move four: keep the topic's vocabulary on the page — food security, climate-smart, irrigation — so each of the four developed ideas collects its two marks.
